pages.title: Overview
pages.md:
# Overview

Munshi's API v1 lets a shop's own website, app or widget show what the shop has published and send the shop requests:
an order, a booking, a hold on a piece, an enquiry.

**Every figure you get is a ledger row. Nothing you send changes the books until the shop approves it.**

- A price, a duration, a count: each comes as a *figure* with a `ref`, the address of the stored cell it was read from.
  `GET …/refs/{snapshot}/{row}/{col}` answers which book row that is. A figure that cannot be traced renders
  "Cannot verify", never a guess.
- Reads come from the shop's latest *release*: the catalogue, services, packages and offers as the owner last
  published them. Stock on hand is never published.
- Writes are requests. An order arrives as a request the shop confirms; a booking request waits for the desk. The
  totals in an order's answer are computed from published price cells, and the shop confirms them.

The API lives under `/api/v1`. Every response carries `Munshi-Api-Version` and an `x-request-id`; quote the request id
when you ask for help.

This is a hackathon build. The shops on the demo are synthetic, payments are recorded and never processed, and messages
to customers are recorded, not sent.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.md:
# Getting started

## 1. Read a published catalogue

Reads need no key. Ask for a shop's site by its slug:

```sh
curl https://<host>/api/v1/sites/prabhave/catalogue?limit=3
```

Each item has its variants, and each variant's price comes back as a figure: whole minor units (paise), the currency,
and the ref of the cell it was read from.

```json
{ "minor": 249900, "currency": "INR", "ref": "⟨snap:…·0·price⟩" }
```

## 2. Install the SDK

Download the tarball from [the SDK page](/developers/sdk), check its sha256, and install it from the file:

```sh
sha256sum munshi-sdk-0.1.0.tgz
npm install ./munshi-sdk-0.1.0.tgz
```

It has no runtime dependencies and runs wherever `fetch` does.

## 3. The first call

```ts
import { createClient, formatMoney } from "@munshi/sdk";

const munshi = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://<host>" });
const page = await munshi.catalogue("prabhave", { limit: 3 });
for (const item of page.data) for (const v of item.variants) console.log(v.name, formatMoney(v.price));
```

`formatMoney` groups the Indian way and shows paise only when there are any. It renders "Cannot verify" for a figure
whose ref does not parse.

## 4. Send a request

Writes need the site's publishable key (`mpk_<slug>_…`), from the shop's settings. The SDK sends it in the
`Authorization` header and adds an `Idempotency-Key` to every write.

```ts
const shop = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://<host>", key: "mpk_prabhave_…" });
const order = await shop.order("prabhave", { shopId, channel: "site", lines: [{ itemId, qtyMilli: 1000 }] });
console.log(order.code); // the code the customer quotes; GET …/orders/{code} shows its steps
```

pages.title: Authentication and errors
pages.md:
# Authentication and errors

## Modes

| Mode | Used by | How |
|---|---|---|
| None | every published read | no header |
| Publishable key | orders, bookings, holds, enquiries, reservations | `Authorization: Bearer mpk_<slug>_…` |
| Secret key | the shop's own drafts and findings | `msk_<slug>_…`; these routes are not open yet |

A publishable key is meant to sit in a web page. It can only send requests the shop approves, and only from the
origins the shop listed for its site. A key that is wrong, revoked or used from another origin answers the same
`not_found` as an unknown route, so a key cannot be probed.

## Origins

A GET without an `Origin` header is served. A browser request from an origin the site does not list answers
`not_found`.

## Idempotency

Every POST and DELETE carries an `Idempotency-Key` header: 8 to 128 of `A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -`. Sending the same key with
the same body again returns the first answer and writes nothing. The same key with a different body answers
`idempotency_mismatch`. Without the header the answer is `idempotency_key_required`.

## Rate limits

Per address: 5 writes in 10 minutes and 120 reads a minute. Per key: 300 writes and 20,000 reads a day. A hold is
limited per device, per address and per stylist and day. Over a limit the answer is `rate_limited` with
`Retry-After`.

## Errors

Every error has one body, its message fixed per code:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "not_found", "message": "Not found.", "fields": [], "requestId": "…" } }
```

`fields` names the request fields that failed their contract, for `invalid`. The full table follows.

pages.title: Figures and refs
pages.md:
# Figures and refs

A figure is a number with its source. There are four shapes:

| Shape | Fields | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Money | `minor`, `currency`, `ref` | a price |
| Integer | `value`, `ref` | a duration in minutes, a number of sessions |
| Derived money | `minor`, `currency`, `from` (refs) | an order's line amount or total, computed from published prices |
| Text, date, time | `text`, `date` or `at`, with `ref` | an item's name |

A `ref` reads `⟨snap:<snapshot id>·<row>·<column>⟩`: the stored snapshot the server read, the row in it, and the
column.

## Tap for source

`GET /api/v1/sites/{slug}/refs/{snapshot}/{row}/{col}` answers whether the cell is one the site's release pins, the
cell itself, which book table and row it came from, and when the release was published:

```json
{ "verified": true, "cell": { "minor": 189900, "currency": "INR", "ref": "⟨snap:…·0·price⟩" }, "source": { "table": "…", "id": "…" }, "publishedAt": "…" }
```

A ref the release does not pin, another shop's, or one that does not parse answers
`{ "verified": false, "label": "Cannot verify" }`. Show that label in place of the number.

## Rules for showing figures

- Render a figure from its own fields; never type a number into your page that did not come as a figure.
- Format money from `minor` with integer arithmetic (the SDK's `formatMoney` does). Never divide into a float.
- Show "Prices from the shop's books · published <date>" near prices, from the site's release.

pages.title: Guides
pages.md:
# Guides

## A catalogue page

Read `catalogue` page by page with its `next` cursor, and show each item's name and price figure. Variants carry their
parent's id. Filter with `category`.

```ts
let cursor: string | undefined;
do {
  const page = await munshi.catalogue("prabhave", { limit: 50, ...(cursor ? { cursor } : {}) });
  render(page.data);
  cursor = page.next ?? undefined;
} while (cursor);
```

## An order widget

The app serves a ready widget. One script and one element put a cart on any page; it reads the catalogue and sends
the order with your publishable key:

```html
<script src="https://<host>/widgets/munshi-order.js"></script>
<munshi-order site="prabhave" key="mpk_prabhave_…" api="https://<host>"></munshi-order>
```

The order arrives at the shop as a request. The customer gets a code and follows its steps at
`GET …/orders/{code}`: step names and times only, never an amount.

## Booking with live slots

For a salon whose site takes live slots: read `services` and `stylists`, then `slots` for a branch, a service and a
date. Hold the slot the customer picks (`hold`), which keeps it for ten minutes, then `book` with the hold's id and
token, the customer's name and phone, and the site's notice and consent versions (from `site`). Release a hold the
customer abandons (`releaseHold`).

```ts
const { slots } = await munshi.slots("elite", { shop, service, date: "2026-11-02" });
const hold = await shop.hold("elite", { shopId: shop, serviceId: service, ...slots[0], botToken });
```

A site without live slots takes `requestBooking`, which the desk confirms.

## Hold a piece

For a shop that sells one-of-a-kind pieces, `reserve` asks the shop to keep a piece for a customer. The shop decides;
nothing is held until it does.

## Offers with codes

`offers` lists the published offers still running, each with its code. Pass the code with an order as `offerCode`. The
order's answer prices the cart from published cells, and the shop confirms the price.

pages.title: Sandbox
pages.md:
# Sandbox

The demo deployment carries two showcase shops built from synthetic data:

| Shop | Slug | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Elite Unisex Salon & Academy (sample menu) | `elite` | two branches, services, stylists, live slots, packages |
| Prabhave (sample catalogue) | `prabhave` | pieces and stitched suits, an offer with a code, orders at each step |

Their reads are open: point any example on these pages at the demo's host. The examples in the reference were
recorded from these two shops.

Requests you send on the demo are kept only as sample values. Payments are never processed and messages are never sent.

pages.title: SDK
pages.md:
# SDK

`@munshi/sdk` is a thin typed client for API v1. The types are generated from the same contracts the server parses
with, so a method's path, query and body are checked at compile time.

- No runtime dependencies. It needs `fetch` (Node 20 or later, or any browser).
- Every money figure renders through `formatMoney(figure, locale)`, integer arithmetic only.
- An error is a `MunshiError` with `status`, `code` and `requestId`.
- The key travels only in the `Authorization` header of a write. Nothing in the client logs.

It is shipped as a tarball from this page, not from npm. Check the sha256 before you install it.

## Changelog

- **0.1.0** — the first release: every published read, the writes (orders, bookings, booking requests, holds,
  enquiries, reservations), `ref`, `formatMoney` and `MunshiError`.
